IsAtom is wrong for preorders. I can make an element which is both IsBot and IsAtom.

import Mathlib

/- def IsAtom.{u_2} : {α : Type u_2} → [inst : Preorder α] → [OrderBot α] → α → Prop :=
fun {α} [Preorder α] [OrderBot α] a => a ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∀ b < a, b = ⊥ -/
#print IsAtom

inductive NotBool where
  | true
  | false

instance : Preorder NotBool where
  le _ _ := True
  lt _ _ := False
  le_refl _ := trivial
  le_trans _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  lt_iff_le_not_ge := by simp

instance : OrderBot NotBool where
  bot := .false
  bot_le _ := trivial

def notatom : Fin 2 × NotBool := (0, .true)

theorem isBot_notatom : IsBot notatom :=
  fun x => ⟨Fin.zero_le x.1, trivial⟩

theorem isAtom_notatom : IsAtom notatom :=
  ⟨nofun, fun a ha => ((isBot_notatom a).not_gt ha).elim⟩

theorem notatom_unique (x : Fin 2 × NotBool) (hx : IsAtom x) : x = notatom :=
  match x with
  | (0, .true) => rfl
  | (1, _) => (isAtom_notatom.1 (hx.right notatom ⟨isBot_notatom _, nofun⟩)).elim

Obviously, the issue is the ≠ in the definition, which is too weak in preorders, and the = in the definition, which is too strong in preorders. What should this be changed to?
(IsCoatom is also wrong)
docs#IsAtom

Aaron Liu said:

What should this be changed to?

IsAtom a := ¬ a ≤ ⊥ ∧ ∀ b < a, b ≤ ⊥ or possibly the neater ⊥ ⋖ a
Personally I would first ask you: What preorders that aren't partial orders do you care about?

Yaël Dillies said:

Aaron Liu said:

What should this be changed to?

IsAtom a := ¬ a ≤ ⊥ ∧ ∀ b < a, b ≤ ⊥ or possibly the neater ⊥ ⋖ a

By the way, I think this can with without assuming OrderBot

Yaël Dillies said:

Personally I would first ask you: What preorders that aren't partial orders do you care about?

Why do you ask? All the preorders I care about now have no atoms, but that doesn't mean there won't be any in the future.
I ask because generality without applicability is merely ruining the soul, said Rabelean, or something like that
Projections in a von Neumann algebra are a preorder under Murray-von Neumann subequivalence. Moreover, a factor is Type I iff this preorder has atoms in the sense Aaron describes.
That's a nice application!
The definition of docs#MeasureTheory.NoAtoms is wrong for essentially the same reason, which I recently noticed.

Aaron Liu said:

By the way, I think this can without assuming OrderBot

I'm not sure what the point of not assuming OrderBot is. If you have an atom, then you automatically have a bot, right?

Jireh Loreaux said:

The definition of docs#MeasureTheory.NoAtoms is wrong for essentially the same reason, which I recently noticed.

Is this what the "NB" in its docstring is trying to convey?
As another example: atoms in the divisibility order (not a partial order if there is a nontrivial unit) should be the docs#Irreducible elements. (assuming we're in a CancelCommMonoid)
Yes, but that's a sort of non-example: We don't use Preorder to talk about divisibility

Yaël Dillies said:

Aaron Liu said:

By the way, I think this can without assuming OrderBot

I'm not sure what the point of not assuming OrderBot is. If you have an atom, then you automatically have a bot, right?

Sometimes there's no canonical choice of bot
Then, sure, use IsBot
but of course you can still talk about atoms and then you don't need the theorem that every bot works equally well for the definition

I'm tempted to use Pi.covBy_iff to characterize irreducible elements in a direct product monoid, but the equivalence between covBy and Irreducible doesn't work if multiplication isn't cancellative. (See the binary version that I already proved.) I wonder if there's anything more general to encompass both. I'm actually interested in showing single _ 1 : Finsupp _ Nat is AddIrreducible, which implies MvPolynomial.X _ is irreducible. (Interesting to note that an additive UniqueFactorizationMonoid is just a group times Finsupp _ Nat.)

Yaël Dillies said:

Yes, but that's a sort of non-example: We don't use Preorder to talk about divisibility

Wait, what do we use?
docs#Dvd

sure
I guess I'm asking, do we not view it as an order at all?
We do in the context of docs#Associates
docs#Associates.instPreorder
I've come back to this now because I unexpectely got a "failed to synthesize instance of type class OrderBot M" while using IsAtom. I think I'm gonna try redefining it as ∃ b, IsBot b ∧ b ⋖ a.
That seems like the correct definition to me
one of the theorems didn't generalize so I decided to try ∃ b, b ⋖ a ∧ ∀ c, c < a → b ≤ c instead

Aaron Liu said:

one of the theorems didn't generalize so I decided to try ∃ b, b ⋖ a ∧ ∀ c, c < a → b ≤ c instead

So it generalises to beyond OrderBot then, since this (to me) reads "a has a (unique up to order-distinguisability) predecessor, which is minimal"?
(Please do correct me if that's not quite right)

Aaron Liu said:

∃ b, b ⋖ a ∧ ∀ c, c < a → b ≤ c

Is that nicer than ∃ b, IsMin b ∧ b ⋖ a?
it's not equivalent, and I thought this would be nicer because it prevents you from making anything an atom by just adding a minimal thing smaller than it
I see... Yeah, my condition is too weak indeed.
opened #40369
Is there a sensible definition that only uses LT? (like docs#CovBy)
with only LT, certain orders become indistinguishable
How does that affect IsAtom?
for example, if I have an order with three elements, such that only a < c and b < c but no other LT relations hold, then I can't tell whether a ≤ b or not
in this case, by this definition, c would be an atom only if a ≤ b
Yes I know, but that doesn't answer my question (or at least I don't see how it does)
then, can you think of a sensible definition that only uses LT?
I haven't tried to, I was wondering if anyone else has an idea or if we've shown such a definition can't exist
Do you have an application in mind for atoms in a preorder? If not, a better fix is to assume PartialOrder in the definition of IsAtom
changing it to PartialOrder wouldn't remove the OrderBot assumption

i suppose there's a weaker assumption which might be sufficient, which is (∃ b, b ⋖ a) ∧ ∀ b, b ⋖ a → ∀ c, ¬ c < b? it does prevent the "we can make any element an atom by inserting a minimal element" property which Aaron didn't want, but loses the "predecessors of atoms are unique (up to order-similarity)" property (which might be relevant, idk)

Edward van de Meent said:

i suppose there's a weaker assumption which might be sufficient, which is (∃ b, b ⋖ a) ∧ ∀ b, b ⋖ a → ∀ c, ¬ c < b? it does prevent the "we can make any element an atom by inserting a minimal element" property which Aaron didn't want, but loses the "predecessors of atoms are unique (up to order-similarity)" property (which might be relevant, idk)

with this definition ⊤ is an atom in WithTop (Nat ⊕ Unit) which doesn't seem right

ah, then perhaps (∃ b, b ⋖ a) ∧ ∀ b, b < a → ∀ c, ¬ c < b (< ipv ⋖ in the rhs of the conjunction)

(or equivalently (assuming only < is transitive), (∃ b, b < a) ∧ (∀ b < a, b ⋖ a))

i do think that it's probably not terribly relevant to generalize this to "lawless orders" like LE (as compared to Preorder), but i also think it's an interesting exercise of "how do i capture this intuition with limited expressiveness", which is a kind i tend to enjoy.

Yaël Dillies said:

Do you have an application in mind for atoms in a preorder? If not, a better fix is to assume PartialOrder in the definition of IsAtom

Yaël, this was discussed upthread. Yes, there are natural examples. IsAtom should not assume PartialOrder.

Aaron Liu said:

changing it to PartialOrder wouldn't remove the OrderBot assumption

Do you have an application in mind for orders without a bottom element?
Oh, this discussion dates a while longer than I remembered

Edward van de Meent said:

ah, then perhaps (∃ b, b ⋖ a) ∧ ∀ b, b < a → ∀ c, ¬ c < b (< ipv ⋖ in the rhs of the conjunction)

(or equivalently (assuming only < is transitive), (∃ b, b < a) ∧ (∀ b < a, b ⋖ a))

I considered suggesting this as well, yesterday. I believe in Preorders another equivalent formulation is (∃ b, b ⋖ a) ∧ ∀ b < a, IsMin b. Any of these seem to be natural if we don't want to assume that the minimal elements below an atom are unique. I don't know whether that is a good or a bad assumption (or whether both make sense).

Yaël Dillies said:

Aaron Liu said:

changing it to PartialOrder wouldn't remove the OrderBot assumption

Do you have an application in mind for orders without a bottom element?

no, but I was surprised when I got an error from failed to synthesize OrderBot
Then I suggest that you hold off generalising, since it isn't clear what the generalisation should be
Atoms are primarily used in the context of bounded lattices
I think this generalization: ∃ b, IsBot b ∧ b ⋖ a is reasonable. But I agree that I don't see any reason to generalize beyond orders that have some bottom element.
Could we give the same treatment to docs#IsAtomic ?
Any progress on this? I'm currently working on adding to_dual tags to these definitions; if we do the redefinition afterwards, it should cut down on work by half.
I'm not so sure about defining it for orders without a bottom anymore, it seems like most people assume a bottom
Yeah but the OrderBot should be part of the predicate rather than a prerequisite to talk about atoms
most things I found only define the concept of atom when the order has a bottom

I have occasionally wanted IsAtom for a preorder without unique bottom element, typically in cases where I do actually have a unique bottom element but it's nontrivial and otherwise unnecessary to prove.
If you want a real example, how about measure-theoretic atoms? Most natural measure spaces do not have a unique bottom set under ≤ᵐ. (Not that this is necessarily something we need in Mathlib.)
